transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, doctor. Well, I'm here because I've been really bothered by this scar on my wrist. I mean, logically, I know the scar is probably not as bad as it looks to me. But... whenever I'm out, like at church or when I'm playing bridge, I just keep feeling like everyone's eyes go right to it. It really feels like it's the very first thing they notice about me now, and it's just been weighing on my mind a lot lately.
When you're thinking about this scar, how much does it interfere with your daily activities or your ability to enjoy things like church or bridge?

Well, it does get in the way a fair amount, actually. For my job—I do bookkeeping—I've actually been late turning in some of my work recently. And outside of work... I've skipped a few of my volunteer commitments for choir and the theater. I just get so caught up trying to figure out long sleeves or just making absolutely sure my wrist won't be noticed, that I end up running out of time or just deciding not to go at all.
When you think about your scar, is your main worry about how the scar actually looks, or is it more about what other people might think of you when they see it?

I'm not really sure how to answer that, to be honest. I haven't really separated the two things in my head. I mean, I don't like how it looks, obviously, but... I don't know if I can say which one is the main worry. It just all sort of blends together for me.
When you picture your scar in your mind, what bothers you the most—the way it looks physically, or the thought that others might judge you for it?

I guess... I still don't really know how to separate those two things. I mean, they're both tied up together. The scar looks awful to me, and because it looks awful, I worry people are staring at it. I can't really pick one over the other. It's just all one big worry.
If I were to look at your wrist right now, would most people say the scar is very noticeable, or would they say it's fairly minor and easy to overlook?

Well, they would probably say it's fairly minor. I mean, deep down, I know the scar on my wrist is probably not as bad as it looks to me. But... it's just hard to remember that when I'm around people. When I’m at church, or sitting at the table for bridge, I just keep feeling like everyone’s eyes go right to it. It feels like it’s the very first thing they notice about me now, even if they wouldn't say it's a big deal.

When you're alone at home, away from other people, do you still find yourself thinking about your scar and worrying about how it looks, or does that worry mainly happen when you're around others or expecting to be around others?

I still think about it when I'm alone, yes. It's not just when I'm at church or with my friends. Even if I'm just sitting in my living room by myself, reading or watching TV, I'll catch sight of it and... well, it just bothers me. I still worry about how it looks, even if there's no one else around to see it. It's just always on my mind.
When you imagine people seeing your scar, what do you think will actually happen as a result? What are you afraid might occur?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't really thought about a specific thing happening. I just... I don't want them to think badly of me, I guess. I just don't like the idea of them noticing it.

When you're worried about your scar, do you find yourself doing specific things repeatedly to try to feel better—like checking how it looks in mirrors, adjusting your clothing over and over, or spending a lot of time trying to cover it up?

Yes, I do a few things before I go out. Before I leave the house, I'll usually check my wrist in the hall mirror a few times. I try pulling my sleeves down over it, or I'll put on a bracelet to see if that covers it up better. Sometimes I'll even ask my husband if it looks obvious, although he always just tells me it's barely there.
